question: Does a MinGW-w64 C++11 static library, linked into a MinGW-w64 Win32 executable, run on Windows 2000 SP4?
result: DECISION (project owner, 2026-11-13): S1 is confirmed on the strength of the Windows 2000 build 2195 (no service pack) trial below. The owner accepts that what runs without a service pack also runs with SP4, because service packs only add or fix exports and keep the ones the executable imports (all 112 imports exist in the RTM DLLs). This is an inference, NOT a measurement: SP4 itself, and its newer msvcrt.dll, were never run. Open, kept open on purpose: the question names Windows 2000 SP4 and the system tested has NO service pack (RTM, build 2195), so SP4 is still untested, and T066 asks for a Windows 2000 SP4 VM, which this VM is not; everything else the question asks (a static C++11 library linked into a Win32 executable, plus the backend self-test) ran on the RTM system; the lead decides the status. TRIAL (2026-11-12): Windows 2000 Professional build 2195, no service pack, English (US), in a VirtualBox 7.2.22 VM (1 vCPU, 168 MB RAM, Guest Additions 6.1.18) on the Windows 11 host; records validation/platforms/windows-2000-x86.json and validation/verdicts/windows-2000-x86-legacy.json (ok_restricted), evidence in validation/evidence/first-trial/windows-2000-x86/, tooling in adr/0003-win2000-vm-unicode-launcher.md. WHAT RAN AND WORKED: the backend self-test (see BACKEND SELF-TEST below) and the i686 Legacy UI executable (694,005 bytes: the MinGW-w64 GCC 13 C++11 static library libloomora.a linked into a Win32 exe with libstdc++ and libgcc static, ADR 0002 shim for GetThreadId) loads and runs. All 112 imports of the executable are exported by the real kernel32.dll 5.0.2191.1, user32.dll 5.0.2180.1, gdi32.dll 5.0.2180.1 and msvcrt.dll 6.1.8637.0 of that system (export tables read; 0 missing), and all 117 functions of the x86 allowlist tools/win2000_imports.json are exported (0 missing); the 12 entries marked verify (TryEnterCriticalSection, the msvcrt.dll start-up internals) are now verified-on-vm for x86 (RTM export tables, not SP4's). The window shows the end-of-life banner, 'Bonjour Coucou', and 'Bonjour Marie' when typed with the virtual keyboard (screenshots); 20 of 20 probe runs: exit 0, display_ms 3 to 13, peak_rss_kb 1084 (checked plausible with memtest and WMI, not a defect), no process left; 15 of 15 reference vectors and 25 of 25 extra hard texts (emoji, CJK, right-to-left, controls, quotes, backslashes, %PATH%, 1,500 characters) round-trip unchanged; exits by itself after 2 s and with Alt+F4. Skipped features on this system: dpi-awareness (user32 does not export SetProcessDPIAware) and dark-mode (no AppsUseLightTheme); GetNativeSystemInfo is absent and the fallback GetSystemInfo is taken; dwmapi.dll is absent. BACKEND SELF-TEST (first attempt failed, fixed, now passes): loomora_selftest cross-built with cmake/toolchains/mingw-w64-win2000-i686.cmake did NOT load on Windows 2000 at first: it imported KERNEL32!GetThreadId (removed by the ADR 0002 shim) and, with or without the shim, four Vista-only functions (InitializeConditionVariable, SleepConditionVariableCS, WakeConditionVariable, WakeAllConditionVariable) from libgcc.a(gthr-win32-cond.o), pulled in by its use of <iostream> (libstdc++ ios_init); the loader refused it (exit status 128, no output), exactly like a control program importing InitializeConditionVariable (selftest-output.txt, the first attempt). The Legacy UI, which links the same libloomora.a but no iostream, was never affected. DECISION taken: keep <iostream> out of core/tests/selftest.cpp (output through std::fputs; std::printf is avoided too because MinGW-w64 maps it to __mingw_vfprintf, which imports msvcrt _lock and _unlock, not on the allowlist) and link the GetThreadId shim into the 32-bit selftest (core/tests/CMakeLists.txt compiles the shim source of the UI; no code duplicated); no extension of the shim, no other toolchain (research R6 fallback 2) was needed. RESULT (2026-11-13): the rebuilt loomora_selftest.exe (sha256 638449ff8e1aeb77a2905d5f5403b2843dc9f766c2f5a138b3bc0574403cdb89, 629,857 bytes) has 67 imports from kernel32 and msvcrt, 0 outside the Windows 2000 SP4 allowlist and 0 not exported by the real DLLs of the VM (117 of 117 allowlist functions exported again); started from a .bat in the guest it printed 'all passed' and ended with exit code 0 (selftest-noiostream-vm-run.txt and .json, selftest-noiostream-imports.txt, selftest-noiostream-vm-exports.txt in validation/evidence/selftest-no-iostream/windows-2000-x86/); the control without the shim still imports GetThreadId and the loader refuses it (errorlevel 128), so the shim stays necessary. The same sources pass on Windows 11 (i686 under WOW64 and x86_64, MinGW-w64), with the host build and ctest, and on Linux (ctest, tools/check_std.py): selftest-noiostream-regression.txt. The selftest covers only the greet vectors, loomora_abi_version and loomora_build_compiler. STILL UNVERIFIED: Windows 2000 SP4 (and the SP4 msvcrt.dll, which is a later build than this RTM one); real hardware instead of VirtualBox; other languages, editions and machines; a person typing, IME, clipboard, a high contrast scheme, DPI above 96; the behaviour of a C++ exception thrown in the static runtime (none was thrown); the 1,000-character EDIT limit by keyboard on this system; Windows 2000 x64 does not exist (N/A); XP and later (S9) and the x64 executable on XP x64 / Server 2003 x64 are not covered.

question: Does modern Clang + osxcross + the 10.6 SDK run on 10.6; does Xcode 5.1.1 build and deploy to iOS 5?

With which toolchain can the backend, the JNI glue and the APK be built for API 9 on armeabi, armeabi-v7a, x86 and arm64-v8a, and how many of those builds can be run on the emulators available (none below API 16)? HISTORY: the first wording of this spike was "does NDK r16b + the scripted APK build run on an Android 2.3 emulator (all four ABIs)?"; it was refuted on 2026-11-14 (NDK r16b has no android-9 platform; r15c has it but its ndk-build raises APP_PLATFORM below 14 to 14) and the question was rewritten to the one above.
result: Confirmed on 2026-11-15 for the rewritten question. HISTORY: status `refuted` on 2026-11-14 for the first wording (NDK r16b + ndk-build); the owner asked to rewrite the question and record `confirmed`, keeping the trace. a CMake toolchain file that drives NDK r15c Clang directly with the android-9 sysroot (android-21 for arm64-v8a) builds libloomora_jni.so and loomora_selftest for armeabi, armeabi-v7a, x86 and arm64-v8a (gnustl static, DT_NEEDED libc.so, plus libdl.so on x86 and arm64-v8a, link with --no-undefined against the API 9 libraries, armeabi needs -latomic); build-tools 36 d8 --min-api 9 and javac -source 8 + aapt + zipalign + apksigner v1 give one APK of the four ABIs (228,623 bytes on 2026-11-14, 228,663 bytes since the package rename to fr.bansan.loomora, same libraries). RUN: only x86, on an Android 4.1.2 (API 16) emulator, the oldest that can be started: loomora_selftest 'all passed', the APK installs and shows the greeting, 15 of 15 reference vectors pass (rerun on the renamed APK on 2026-11-15, API 16 and API 24, see the verdicts). NOT DONE, and not possible with the emulators of this project: running on Android 2.3 to 4.0 (API 9 to 15) and any ARM ABI (no ARM system image or device). The claim 'runs on Android 2.3' is neither confirmed nor refuted, T068 stays unticked and T091 stays partial. UPDATE 2026-11-15 (T068 check): the rewritten question is answered by this record, ADR 0016 and the platform android-4.1.2-x86 (Legacy verdict ok_restricted, selftest-x86-api16.txt 'all passed', 15 of 15 vectors), so T068 is ticked; the sentence 'T068 stays unticked' above was written before the rewrite and is kept as history. T091 stays partial.
fallback: NDK r15c + CMake toolchain file + scripted APK build instead of NDK r16b + ndk-build (ADR 0016)

question: Does the Web JavaScript path (no WebAssembly) run on a Windows-2000-compatible Firefox, and with which Emscripten? HISTORY: the first wording of this spike was "Does the JavaScript build run on IE 9 / Firefox 8 / Chrome 15 / Safari 5.1 / Opera 11.5; modern Emscripten or fastcomp 1.39.20?"; Internet Explorer up to 9 was refuted as a target on 2026-11-15 (no typed arrays: Emscripten 1.39.20 fastcomp needs them, Emscripten 1.29.12 plain arrays crashes on 64-bit integer arithmetic in libc++, the current Emscripten emits ECMAScript 2021 syntax; see the result below) and the owner dropped IE up to 9, keeping one lowest testable browser, so the question was rewritten to the one above.
result: Confirmed on 2026-11-15 for the rewritten question. HISTORY: status `open` until 2026-11-15 for the first wording (five browsers, none run), then rewritten and recorded `confirmed` once Firefox 10 ran the JavaScript path, keeping the earlier result below unchanged. FIREFOX 10 RUN (2026-11-15, validation/evidence/web-firefox/web-firefox-10-windows-2000-x86/, verdict validation/verdicts/web-firefox-10-windows-2000-x86-legacy.json, procedure validation/procedures/web.md): Firefox 10.0 (build ID 20120129021758) on Windows 2000 build 2195 without service pack, in the VirtualBox VM 'Windows 2000' with 168 MB of RAM, loads the Web Legacy page over HTTP from the host (http://10.0.2.2:<port>/index.html?probe=1&input=...&platform=web-firefox-10-windows-2000-x86&post=1) and runs the JavaScript build of the C++11 backend produced by Emscripten 1.39.20 FASTCOMP (loomora.js, 91,529 bytes, ECMAScript 3, memory image embedded): 'core' is cpp-js and the HTTP log shows loomora.js and never loomora.wasm; the page shows 'Bonjour Coucou' and, with 'Marie' typed from keyboard scancodes, 'Bonjour Marie' (screenshot); 15 reference vectors run, 14 pass, and control_characters differs only by its line feed, which an HTML text field removes in every browser (a current Chrome does the same; a property of the field, not of the JavaScript path); the probe records validate against tools/check_probe.py in every run; display_ms 124 to 143 ms; no firefox.exe process left after Alt+F4. The 'Emscripten' half of the question is answered for this browser: fastcomp 1.39.20 works; the current Emscripten 7.0.0 JavaScript build was not run in a browser (its ECMAScript 2021 syntax rules it out for Firefox 10 by reading, as before). NOT VERIFIED, and not claimed: any other old browser (Firefox 4 to 9, Chrome 15, Safari 5.1, Opera 11.5, IE 10 and 11), Windows 2000 with SP4, real hardware, a person typing, memory (Firefox 10 has no performance.memory), a cold start of Firefox; the WebAssembly path was not run on any old browser (Firefox 10 has none). Under the PoC rule (success on the lowest testable browser stands for newer ones) the JavaScript path is validated; the ADR that research R8 asks for is NOT written yet. EARLIER RESULT (kept): PARTLY ANSWERED, status kept `open` because the question names five browsers and none was available (no old browser was run; the browser part is NOT TESTED). ANSWERED (2026-11-15, WSL Ubuntu 24.04, node, evidence validation/evidence/web-s5/linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64/): the backend builds for the Web as strict C++11 with the toolchain files cmake/toolchains/emscripten-wasm.cmake and emscripten-js.cmake (presets web-wasm and web-js, bridge/wasm/exports.txt = the six loomora_* functions). (1) Current Emscripten 7.0.0 (clang 24): -sWASM=0 -sLEGACY_VM_SUPPORT=1 is still ACCEPTED, with only the warning 'WASM=0 is deprecated (under consideration for removal, emscripten issue 27608)'; it builds a JavaScript-only loomora.js (61,551 bytes, no .wasm), which starts with the WebAssembly global deleted and passes the 43 checks of tools/trials/web-node/s5-node-driver.js (the six exports, loomora_greet of 'Coucou' gives 'Bonjour Coucou', all 31 greet vectors of core/tests/vectors.json, probe record with core kinds 2 and 3) and the backend self-test (ctest). BUT the generated glue is not ES5: acorn parses it only as ECMAScript 2021 (arrow functions, async functions, optional chaining, globalThis, default parameters), so its first token already is a syntax error for any engine without those features; LEGACY_VM_SUPPORT=1 only lowers the MIN_*_VERSION settings and does not change the syntax. So the current Emscripten JavaScript path cannot be loaded by IE 9, Firefox 8, Chrome 15, Safari 5.1 or Opera 11.5 (static reading of the syntax, not a browser run). The WebAssembly build of 7.0.0 (loomora.js 14,152 bytes + loomora.wasm 23,971 bytes) passes the same 43 checks and fails as expected when the WebAssembly global is removed. (2) Emscripten 1.39.20 with the upstream (wasm) backend, -sWASM=0 -sLEGACY_VM_SUPPORT=1: builds (86,727 bytes + 2,018 bytes loomora.js.mem), the glue parses as ECMAScript 3, passes the 43 checks and the self-test, also with the WebAssembly global removed. (3) Emscripten 1.39.20 FASTCOMP (installed from a clone of emsdk checked out at 3.1.29, because the current emsdk refuses fastcomp): builds true asm.js (86,586 bytes + 2,093 bytes .mem), ECMAScript 3 syntax, passes the same 43 checks and the self-test without WebAssembly. emcc warns that fastcomp is deprecated and that ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH disables some asm.js optimisations. Facts the Web UI must handle: the backend needs C++ exceptions (-fexceptions, set by the toolchain; with Emscripten's default a throw aborts the module and the first greet vector that throws killed the run); loomora_probe_record takes an int64 (rss_kb), a BigInt in the WebAssembly build of 7.0.0 and two 32-bit numbers (low, high) in every JavaScript build; list settings of 1.39.20 accept only JSON arrays, so exports.txt and runtime-methods.txt are JSON arrays; the asm.js builds write the memory initialiser to a separate loomora.js.mem file (--memory-init-file 0 would inline it; not tried). The 1.39.20 glue polyfills Math.imul and Math.clz32 but NOT typed arrays (Int8Array, Uint8Array, Float64Array are used as is), which Internet Explorer 9 does not have: whether IE 9 runs it is unanswered. NOT ANSWERED, NOT TESTED: whether any of the five browsers (IE 9, Firefox 8, Chrome 15, Safari 5.1, Opera 11.5) runs any of these builds, and the speed of the typed-array emulation on IE 9. The choice between the current Emscripten (ruled out by its ES2021 syntax unless a transpiler is added, which was not tried) and 1.39.20 (upstream or fastcomp) for the browsers below ES2021 therefore rests on syntax and a Node run, not on a browser: the ADR that R8 asks for is NOT written until a browser answers (T070 stays unticked, T086 keeps its choice open). ES3 FOLLOW-UP (2026-11-15, WSL Ubuntu 24.04, node, evidence validation/evidence/web-es3/linux-ubuntu-24.04-x86_64/): question: can the JavaScript path run on a browser with no typed arrays and no ES5 library (Internet Explorer 6 to 9) and with which Emscripten version and flags?  ANSWER: NO WORKING COMBINATION FOUND for the C++11 backend; one exact blocker per version. (1) Emscripten 1.39.20 fastcomp (-sWASM=0 -sLEGACY_VM_SUPPORT=1 --memory-init-file 0): there is no mode without typed arrays: USE_TYPED_ARRAYS is not a setting any more (emcc: 'Attempt to set a non-existent setting', ChangeLog: removed in 1.30.6) and ASM_JS=0 is refused ('ASM_JS can only be set to either 1 or 2'), so the output is asm.js on HEAP8/HEAP32/HEAPF64 views. What works: loomora.js is 91,529 bytes with the memory image embedded (--memory-init-file 0, no loomora.js.mem), acorn parses it as ECMAScript 3 (es-level.js), and with only WebAssembly deleted it passes the 43 checks of s5-node-driver.js (greet 'Coucou' gives 'Bonjour Coucou', 31 greet vectors, probe records). What fails: with ArrayBuffer, DataView and the eight typed array constructors deleted from the global object it stops at load ('ReferenceError: ArrayBuffer is not defined'); the file calls new ArrayBuffer, Int8Array, Uint8Array, Int16Array, Uint16Array, Int32Array, Uint32Array, Float32Array and Float64Array (21 constructor calls). On IE 6 to 8 a polyfill cannot help (no index access on an object that is not an array, and the views of one buffer would have to alias), on IE 9 a polyfill would have to be a byte-array emulation behind plain index access, which was not tried. ES5 library feature the glue needs (trace run under node, LOOMORA_ES5=trace): only Function.prototype.bind, 52 calls, the first one console.log.bind of the node environment code; with it deleted the module stops there; a web environment build was not traced. The glue itself is ES3 syntax. (2) Emscripten 1.29.12, the last release that still has the old non-fastcomp compiler core (EMCC_FAST_COMPILER=0, stock clang/LLVM 3.3, Python 2.7.18 built from source, target i386-pc-linux-gnu, three local patches listed in the log) and USE_TYPED_ARRAYS=0 -s ASM_JS=0: a C hello world builds (335,995 bytes, ES3 per acorn) and prints 'hi 42' with every typed array global deleted, so the mode did exist; its glue still calls Array.prototype.forEach in the file system start-up (ES5 library; with it deleted the run stops at '[ERRNO_CODES.ENOENT].forEach is not a function'), and also filter, Date.now, Function.prototype.bind and Object.defineProperties in a trace run (part of these calls come from node itself). BLOCKER: a C++11 program that uses std::string builds and prints 'Bonjour Coucou 14' with the same compiler in the default typed array mode (2.1 MB, non-asm.js), but with USE_TYPED_ARRAYS=0 the compiler core crashes ('Internal compiler error in src/compiler.js ... TypeError: Cannot read property 0 of undefined' in isIntImplemented, after 'Warning: 64 bit XOR - precision limit may be hit'): 64-bit integer arithmetic in the libc++ code (std::string) is not implemented without typed arrays. The Loomora backend (core/src/*.cpp) fails the same way, with or without -O1 --llvm-lto 1, so no loomora.js exists in this mode. (3) Emscripten 1.30.5 and later fastcomp releases: NOT RUN (no fastcomp LLVM was built); read from the source of the tag: emcc asserts 'fastcomp assumes ta2' (USE_TYPED_ARRAYS == 2) and 'ASM_JS must be enabled in fastcomp', and emscripten.py prints 'Non-fastcomp compiler is no longer available' (the old compiler core is gone from 1.30.0), so the plain-array mode cannot exist from 1.30.0 on. Versions before 1.29.12 were not tried (the same 64-bit limitation is expected but not verified). NOT VERIFIED: any browser, IE 6 to 9 in particular; the ES5 library features of a web (not node) environment build; whether a plain-array build could work for a backend written in C without libc++ (loomora_probe_record also takes an int64); a typed-array emulation by post-processing the asm.js heap accesses into function calls (not tried). CONSEQUENCE FOR THE OWNER: with this toolchain the JavaScript path stays at IE 10 (typed arrays, no WebAssembly) or, if a polyfilled IE 9 is acceptable, at the browsers that have typed arrays natively; IE 6 to 8, and IE 9 without a typed array emulation, need either a second implementation of the core in plain JavaScript, a backend without libc++ and without 64-bit integers compiled with Emscripten 1.29.12 plain arrays, or being dropped from the Web target; no toolchain file for them was added because none works. Status stays `open`. ADR 0017 (2026-11-15) now records the decision: WebAssembly path with Emscripten 7.0.0, JavaScript path with Emscripten 1.39.20 fastcomp, Internet Explorer up to 9 dropped.
fallback: Emscripten 1.39.20 fastcomp (-sWASM=0, --memory-init-file 0) for the JavaScript path, loaded only by browsers without WebAssembly (fallback web-js-instead-of-wasm); confirmed by Firefox 10.0 on Windows 2000; the current Emscripten is kept for the WebAssembly path. Earlier wording: Emscripten 1.39.20 (-sWASM=0, upstream backend or fastcomp) instead of the current Emscripten for the JavaScript path, if a browser confirms it; not decided, no browser tested

question: Does the backend compile with strict C++11 under GCC and Clang and export only C symbols, with every exception caught at the C boundary?
result: Confirmed on Linux (WSL Ubuntu 24.04, libstdc++): tools/check_std.py passes with g++ 13.3.0 and clang++ 23.1.5. Checked for each: all 6 core/src/*.cpp compile with -std=c++11 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra -Werror; loomora.h compiles as C89 (-std=c89 -pedantic-errors, gcc 13.3.0 / clang 23.1.5) and as C++98; a shared library built with -fvisibility=hidden exports exactly the 6 loomora_* C functions (nm -D --defined-only), with the C++ runtime linked dynamically and statically (-static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc); core/tests/boundary_check.cpp makes every allocation of every loomora_* call fail in turn (28 failures injected with GCC, 30 with Clang) and no exception escapes. Finding: -fvisibility=hidden alone is NOT enough, libstdc++ marks namespace std as default visibility and std template instantiations leaked into the exports (4 with g++, 16 with clang++); fixed with a link-time export list (core/loomora.map, core/loomora.exp for macOS) that CMake and check_std.py apply to the shared library. Not checked: strict C++11 with clang on Windows (clang 23.1.1 uses the MSVC STL, which needs C++14: the checker reports it as skipped; only the C89/C++98 header checks ran there), libc++, MSVC, Windows DLL exports (__declspec macros untested), macOS exports (loomora.exp untested), and the old compilers of the oldest platforms (S1-S4).

HISTORY: the first wording asked "does Compose accept minSdk 21?"; the answer is no (the pinned libraries declare minSdk 23), so that wording is refuted as stated; the question was rewritten to the one above at the owner's request.
result: Confirmed on 2026-11-15 for the rewritten question. HISTORY: recorded `refuted` on 2026-11-15 for the first wording (Compose accepts minSdk 21), then rewritten and recorded `confirmed` at the owner's request, keeping this trace. WinUI half, CONFIRMED: WinUI 3 (C#, Windows App SDK 2.6.5, unpackaged and framework-dependent, .NET SDK 10.0.404) calls the C++11 loomora.dll through LibraryImport (no C++/CLI, no C++/WinRT) on Windows 11 x64: loomora.dll is built by MSVC 14.52.37025 (cl.exe 19.52.37029, /MT, cl.exe's default /std:c++14 since MSVC has no /std:c++11, the sources stay C++11), exports exactly the six loomora_* functions and imports KERNEL32.dll only (x64 and ARM64 built; ARM64 not run). The ABI check, the greeting, the end-of-life test and the probe record all come from the DLL; 15 of 15 reference vectors pass through the WinUI window in probe mode, for the net10.0 build and for the net8.0 build (Windows App SDK 2.6.5 accepts net8.0, no older SDK needed); the net8 build starts on a machine that has only .NET 10 or only .NET 11 with RollForward Major. Published folder 37.8 MB (zip 9.9 MB) with only the WinUI and Runtime components of the SDK (81.9 MB with the Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK metapackage). Not run: Windows 10 1809, ARM64 execution. Evidence validation/evidence/winui3/windows-11-x64/, verdict validation/verdicts/windows-11-x64-modern.json, procedure validation/procedures/windows.md part C. Android half, REFUTED: Compose with the pinned AndroidX versions (AGP 9.5.1, Gradle 9.9.1, Kotlin 2.3.21, Compose BOM 2026.09.00, activity-compose 1.13.0) does NOT accept minSdk 21: `python tools/build.py android modern --min-sdk 21` fails in the manifest merger, androidx.compose.animation:animation-core-android:1.12.1 declares minSdk 23 (evidence validation/evidence/android-modern/android-7.0-x86_64/spike-s8-minsdk21.txt). tools:overrideLibrary would hide the check but may fail at run time and was not tried. The decided floor 24 stays: minSdk 24 builds and runs on an API 24 x86_64 emulator (15 of 15 vectors, validation/verdicts/android-7.0-x86_64-modern.json).
fallback: Compose minSdk 24 instead of 21 (decided floor; the Android Legacy UI covers API 9 to 23); WinUI half needs none

question: Do Windows 7 -> 11 accept the Windows 2000-targeted Win32 executable (all versions)?
What do GitHub-hosted runners provide for the continuous integration (runner images, KVM, Docker, ARM64, submodule checkout, caching), and what has to stay a local run?
result: OPEN. ANSWERED by reading GitHub's documentation and the runner-images readmes on 2026-11-15 (URLs and dates in ADR 0018): the hosted runner labels and sizes (ubuntu-22.04, ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-24.04-arm, windows-latest = Windows Server 2025, windows-11-arm, macos-26 arm64, macos-15-intel: 4 vCPU / 16 GB for Linux and Windows on public repositories, 3 vCPU / 7 GB for macOS arm64); standard hosted runners, arm64 ones included, are free and unlimited on public repositories; the image contents (Ubuntu 24.04: Docker 28.0.4, CMake 3.31.6, GCC 12 to 14, Clang 16 to 18, Python 3.12, Xvfb, NDK 27, 29 and 30, no gtkmm and no libx11-dev so the jobs apt-get them; Windows 2025: Visual Studio 2022 17.14, .NET 8 to 11, MSYS2 not on PATH, Chrome and Firefox; Windows 11 ARM: Visual Studio 2022 with the ARM64 tools; macOS 26: Xcode 26.0.1 to 26.6 and iOS 26.2, 26.4 and 26.5 simulators, no Emscripten); KVM for the Android emulator is documented for Linux runners (changelog 2024-04-02: udev rule, 2 vCPU and up); Docker is on the Linux image; the cache limits (10 GB per repository, 7 days); ubuntu-22.04 is deprecated from 2026-09-17 and retired 2027-04-17 (runner-images issue 14254); OWNER DECISION 2026-11-15: hosted runners only (both repositories are public, so no self-hosted runner), and what they cannot run (VirtualBox virtual machines, manylinux1 CentOS 5.11 needing vsyscall=emulate, legacy Apple systems) is a local run recorded in the records, not a CI job. ANSWERED BY A REAL RUN, 2026-11-15, push of branch feat/ci1 (commit 9a7a86c): https://github.com/bansan85/loomora/actions/runs/43712716870 (attempt 2, all jobs green: changes, linux on ubuntu-22.04, ubuntu-24.04 and ubuntu-24.04-arm, linux variants, gate; the docs job was skipped by design because the push changed code). FINDING: attempt 1 failed only because the commit named by the docs submodule pointer was not on GitHub yet (it had been pushed to the local sibling repository only): the pointer of the main repository must be reachable on github.com/bansan85/loomora-docs, so loomora-docs is pushed first. PROVEN for a push run: actions/checkout v7.0.1 with submodules: recursive resolves the relative URL ../loomora-docs to https://github.com/bansan85/loomora-docs (log: "Submodule 'docs/implementation' (https://github.com/bansan85/loomora-docs) registered") and checks out the pointed commit 8565c9f and third_party/catch2; no token is needed for the two public repositories. PROVEN: the Linux packages of docs/building/README.md install with apt-get on the three images (about 30 to 50 s) and python3 tools/verify.py quick passes 9 of 9 on each (ctest 2/2 with the Catch2 tests, 15/15 vectors through the Xlib and the gtkmm UIs on a private Xvfb display, check_std, check_ui_logic, records, diff_verdicts, run_vectors self-test), with no SKIP, so Xvfb and both UIs work on ubuntu-24.04-arm too. Durations of the jobs: ubuntu-22.04 1 min 16 s, ubuntu-24.04 1 min 34 s, ubuntu-24.04-arm 1 min 32 s (apt-get 31 to 37 s, verify.py 37 to 50 s), variants 3 min 04 s.
